"In 1981, the viral element SV40 was reported to enhance gene expression -- the very 1st known enhancer! In 1983, the 1st eukaryotic enhancer was discovered.   Today, researchers like Jefferson postdoc @USER are  studying the role of enhancers in the evolution of longevity!"

"#JeffTakeover   While changes to gene regulation can have adverse affects on development and lead to very severe phenotypes, gene regulatory variation is also a significant driver of evolution!"

"Gene regulatory elements can be very close to the gene they control (proximal elements) or they can be incredibly far away (distal elements)   One active area of research is understanding how distal elements contact gene promoters through chromatin looping! #JeffTakeover HTTPURL"

"Also at Jefferson, Dr. Maria Ramirez's lab studies the role of non-coding RNAs in the regulation of lung epithelial genes. Studying this developmental process will pave the way for therapies against childhood and adult lung diseases! #JeffTakeover"

"Recent work from @USER at Jefferson has shown how the protein ARID1B regulates developmental gene expression. Loss of ARID1B binding at multiple gene regulatory elements leads to a series of phenotypes known as Coffin-Siris Syndrome #JeffTakeover  HTTPURL"

"#JeffTakeover  The development of vertebrate cells, tissues, organs and body plans requires very precise control of gene expression. Changes to the time and location of gene expression can lead to changes in cell fate or even incomplete development of an organ."

"One of the reasons this is so interesting is that for a long time, non-coding DNA was considered "junk". I personally remember learning about "junk DNA" in high school. Only recently have we begun to understand how to decode it. ##JeffTakeover HTTPURL"

"Gene regulatory elements -- enhancers, promoters, or repressors -- are made up of binding sites for transcription factor proteins.   These DNA-protein interactions are key to mediating gene expression, like in this schematic from Scitable HTTPURL"
"Gene regulation can happen at the level of transcription or the level of translation and I definitely don't think one is cooler or more interesting than the other. HTTPURL"

"For any given gene, we might like to know 1) where is it expressed 2) when it is expressed 3) the duration of its expression 4) how much is it expressed and so on   Enter gene regulatory elements: the non-protein-coding pieces of DNA that provide instructions for gene expression."

"Once the timer goes off you have a 5 minute break to do whatever youd like. And after the 5 minute break you work again and again until you reach your longer break then repeat again! There are many free Pomodoro Timers available online or you could also set a manual timer."

"I can admit it. I, like other people I know, work better outside of the home. Its something about knowing I need to finish a task so that I can go home that adds a little fire to finish. My go to for #workingfromhome is the Pomodoro Technique!! HTTPURL"

"The Pomodoro Technique in short: 25 min work period ➡️ 5 minute break 🔁repeat then a longer break period after completing multiple work periods. The idea is when you start your timer you work-not check your phone/email, not add something to your cart, not grab a snack-JUST WORK!"

"Decide if you want to knock out the hardest tasks first (making the other tasks feel more doable) or if you should start with an easy task first to get the ball rolling. If youre feeling unmotivated or overwhelmed starting the day with an easier task may be the way to go."

"Now for procrastination-If youre having a hard time getting started the key is to just start! One trick to beat procrastination is commit to 5, 10, or 15 distraction-free minutes. Once you get the ball rolling it is easier to keep going."

"Mix in more enjoyable tasks or activities as well on unmotivated days so that you feel rewarded with something you want to do (or are more motivated to do) once you knock out a less enjoyable task.   #JeffTakeover #workingfromhome"

"While #workingfromhome dont forget it is important to take time for self care. While you do want to get things done dont forget to plan time for healthy activities too like exercising, cooking and eating, and checking in with friends and loved ones.  #JeffTakeover"
"Okay, so maybe you do really want to organize things at home. Plan that time too! Just dont forget to stick to your schedule and do work at the times youve set for work."

"Do you end up on your phone too much? Try using the Do Not Disturb feature to avoid all the random notifications while you're working or try a productivity app that can block distracting apps and notifications on your phone during your work time."

"So as you plan your day one tip to overcome distraction is removing things that are distracting and setting a specific time for them. Turn off social media, TV/movies, YouTube, and other distracting things while you work. Plan breaks for them or use them after your "work day"."
"Planning is important, but let's face it there are a couple elephants in the room-distraction and procrastination. HTTPURL"
